text: Install-path symlink write symmetry (wave-5 security P3 advisory, out of 045-S uninstall/serve scope). The uninstall and read paths now reject a symlinked or junction .gitignore and validate MCP config candidates via is_reparse_point/validate_path, but the INSTALL write paths still follow a pre-existing symlink: add_gitignore_entry does fs read_to_string plus fs write on .gitignore, and generate_mcp_config/write_json write .mcp.json and can traverse a symlinked .vscode parent. If an attacker plants a symlink at .gitignore or .mcp.json before the developer runs install, install would read or overwrite the external target, escaping the workspace on the write path. Fix: gate the install writers with the same is_reparse_point/validate_path containment guard used on the uninstall and serve side, with regression tests. Source: PR 90 wave-5 Security Reviewer finding, confidence 0.63.

Short-circuit source_has_ingestible_content in src/workspace/serve_discovery.rs (line ~333). It currently eagerly walks the entire source tree via WalkDir, collects every format-matching relative path, then calls graphtor_core::acquire::filter_files once and checks non-empty. The caller (serve auto-discovery ServeMode classification) only needs a boolean, so serve startup pays a full traversal and retains memory proportional to document count, and background sync scans the same tree again. Optimization: compile the format matcher and include/exclude glob matcher once, then return true as soon as the first file passes BOTH the format check AND the include/exclude filter. Care needed: filter_files is currently a batch API, so a correct short-circuit must apply the glob include/exclude semantics per file (empty include = include all, exclude wins) without changing which files count as ingestible. Add a regression test asserting an excluded-only tree returns false and that a large tree returns true after inspecting only the first eligible file. Source: PR 90 wave-7 Copilot performance finding on serve_discovery.rs:342. Deferred from 045-S under the review-cycle hard stop because it is genuinely new performance scope, not a correctness or containment regression.

cmd_upgrade lacks the is_reparse_point containment guard that install/uninstall/serve now have. In src/main.rs cmd_upgrade acquires WorkspaceLock::acquire(workspace_dir, force_unlock) on a workspace resolved by find_workspace_dir, which matches .graphtor via candidate.is_dir() (follows symlinks/junctions). If .graphtor is a reparse point pointing outside the project, upgrade's lock acquire and --force-unlock create/remove/replace graphtor.lock inside the external target (out-of-workspace mutation), the same containment class fixed for install (W7-1) and uninstall (W7-2) on PR 90. Fix: add if graphtor_core::path::is_reparse_point(and ws_dir) bail before the acquire in cmd_upgrade, mirroring the install/uninstall guards, plus a regression test planting a symlinked .graphtor and asserting upgrade fails closed and the linked target lock is untouched. Source: PR 90 wave-7 Security Reviewer finding, confidence 0.72, P3 advisory. Deferred from 045-S because cmd_upgrade is out of the W7-1/W7-2 declared scope; prioritized high for immediate next-shipment attention because it is a security containment gap.

Spike: read-only-serve cross-process coordination design. Covers deferred Copilot PR90 review items F2 (status/query read-only cross-process open hinging on the read-only-serve x-process design) and F6 (stale-lock liveness and ownership). Redesigning cross-process liveness/ownership using the filesystem-readonly-attribute as a lock is beyond the single-developer local 045-S shipment scope; investigate an ownership/liveness model before changing serve open semantics.

Served-alias handling follow-up for serve auto-discovery (deferred from Copilot PR90 review). Evaluate whether served database aliases need explicit canonicalization or reporting beyond the current dedup union.
